Thanks @keithamus and @annevk for the thoughtful feedback.

Given the overlap with `InputRange` in the [Richer Text Fields explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/richer-text-fields.explainer/#adding-a-new-range-type), we suggest treating `FormControlRange` as a concrete proposal within that broader effort. We’ll update our explainer to clarify that the range type is live, add examples for value changes, and reference the Richer Text Fields explainer directly to avoid duplication.

We’re also considering a rename (e.g. `ElementRange`, as @annevk suggested) to better reflect extensibility and avoid confusion with `InputRange` (since the name may imply it only applies to `<input>` elements).

Please let us know if this direction sounds good to you, as we’d like to align before bringing this to wider review. Thanks!

We synced with @keithamus offline, and he’s aligned with the current direction. We're proceeding with the name `FormControlRange` for now to match the work done so far (explainer and initial Chromium implementation), but if there are objections or a strong preference for a broader name (e.g., `ElementRange`), please let us know and we can update it. Thanks!
At which point would FormControlRange be updated if it is like a live Range? After beforeinput, but before input event?  What about key events, or dnd etc?

FormControlRange should update only when an edit is committed to the control’s value: after the `beforeinput` default action (if not canceled) and before `input`. We want this to mirror how `Range` updates on DOM mutations. It does not update on raw keydown/keyup. Paste and drag-and-drop trigger a single update once the final text is inserted. IME updates only when text is committed, not during preview. Programmatic edits update immediately, and if `beforeinput` is canceled there’s no update.

I'd rather see extending `Range` to work with selection across shadow boundaries in general, and make it work with form controls. If we're going with `FormControlRange`, we need a support for form control custom elements.

> I'd rather see extending `Range` to work with selection across shadow boundaries in general, and make it work with form controls. If we're going with `FormControlRange`, we need a support for form control custom elements.

@rniwa Thanks for the feedback. I know you and @dandclark discussed [this in another thread](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1404#issuecomment-3353952451), so I’ll summarize it here to keep the discussion in one place:

Extending `Range` to cross shadow boundaries or into form controls would mean changing some long-standing assumptions about how it works, like DOM boundary constraints, mutation behavior, and what methods such as `selectNodeContents()` should do for elements with internal value models. That would add quite a bit of complexity and ambiguity into a core API that’s been stable for a long time.

`FormControlRange` keeps things simpler and more contained. It’s a separate, live `AbstractRange` subclass that works entirely within the value space of `<input>` and `<textarea>`. This preserves encapsulation while still enabling `Range` style geometry and selection APIs, without exposing or touching the control’s internal DOM.

We agree that supporting form-associated custom elements is a good next step for future work. Once the model is solid for native text controls, we can explore letting custom elements support these capabilities while preserving encapsulation. We’ve (very) briefly noted it as a possible follow-up in the [explainer](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/FormControlRange/explainer.md#extending-to-custom-elements-and-potential-renaming).

Very excited to see work towards solving this issue — that’s a major limitation of the current state of the Custom Highlight API!

Reading through the explainer, I wonder if web compat research was done before ruling out the first approach (simply letting `setStart()` and `setEnd()` to work). Enabling existing primitives to just work instead of introducing new ones that authors need to learn is usually a more ergonomic solution.

Another (minor) concern with this proposed API is what happens if down the line we have form controls encapsulating multiple text fields?

Possibly too late for considering other ways to solve this problem, but just to throw an idea out there, what if instead of solving the problem in `Range` we solved it by giving regular `Range` objects a DOM node to hook onto? E.g. a property that exposed a `Node` element or a `NodeList`, containing a (virtual) text node for `<input>` and `<textarea>`. This has the benefit of being extensible to more complex structures in the future, though it may be slower when there is no actual text node in the control's shadow DOM and it needs to be fabricated at runtime (though that can be done lazily) and kept in sync. This could also pave the way for other elements that display UI text that does not correspond to any actual DOM element (accessible to the page author).

Based on the discussion at TPAC to ensure this is compatible with custom elements and future needs, I think we should explore a new range whose start and end container are fully internal. So they don't return the host, they just return null.

That way it can be constructed at any level of nesting and just passed to outer layers without fear of exposing encapsulated nodes. This does mean that creating it needs to be on `<input>`, `<textarea>`, and custom elements directly. The former two through dedicated API and custom elements through API web developers can add themselves.

So API surface-wise you'd have:

- `OpaqueRange extends AbstractRange` (and `AbstractRange`'s `startContainer` and `endContainer` need to be nullable). (An alternative might be that we create `AbstractAbstractRange` which doesn't have `startContainer` and `endContainer`. We're not entirely sure what's better.)
- `new OpaqueRange({ startContainer: encapsulatedNode, ... })` (possibly `ShadowRange`, `RemoteRange`)
- `<input>.getValueRange(startOffset, endOffset)`
- `<textarea>.getValueRange(startOffset, endOffset)`

I don't think that this range should expose `toString()`. That's more a feature of selection, not ranges. If ranges supported that it would be very different from selection as it would be node-tree-based and not layout-based.

Commented the API shape on the PR. Overall I think that looks quite reasonable, but some tweaks would be good.
(I don't personally really like the name OpaqueRange, it is somehow too vague, but I don't have better suggestions.)

Re: the offsets discussion today, I wrote up a proposal for the idea I suggested, since I don't think I explained it well in the meeting: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12475

> This could also address the `OpaqueRange` dilemma discussed today: instead of exposing `startOffset` and `endOffset`, which have a different meaning depending on whether the boundaries are element nodes, or contorting them to mean something _different_ for `OpaqueRange`, only expose these high-level attributes which have the same meaning regardless — and if we want to expose the rest later, we still can, and these are _independently_ useful.

I think the `OpaqueRangeController` is a good design that answers the custom element case nicely. I think we might want to consider keeping `disconnect()` on the range so that consumers can properly discard an OpaqueRange when done with it, but the custom element should somehow be notified of that so it can tidy up and prevent doing work for controllers it doesn't need to; so perhaps via an event? `interface OpaqueRangeController : EventTarget`? Alternatively `readonly boolean OpaqueRange.connected` which can be checked just-in-time.

When it comes to Custom Elements I think we should avoid being over prescriptive. If we retain `startOffset`/`endOffset` it is up to custom element authors to ascribe meaning to them. I think your image gallery provides a perfect example of this. As such I don't think we should worry about adding geometry callbacks or auto clamping. Custom Elements can do all of this in script, without much issue. I'll stress: ultimately all of this design is not something out of the realms of custom element authors today, so there is less burden on us to provide a satisfactory interface just for this; yes it is nice, but really `OpaqueRangeController`/`OpaqueRange` for custom element authors is little more than `WeakSet`/`{ startOffset, endOffset }`. The more semantics we attach to it the higher the risk we deviate from that, rendering the feature less useful for custom element authors, as they'll just retreat back to what's possible in script today.

I think `OpaqueRange` should retain `startOffset`/`endOffset`. I don't think `textStart`/`textEnd` make sense here, that feels like "another thing" (i.e. not an `AbstractRange` subclass). `valueFromRange()` probably makes sense but I would like us to make sure we do not add a proliferation of new APIs around what should be a simple feature. If we start finding use cases which need new APIs we need to consider what can be coalesced.

I'm not sure about `disconnect()` still. Wouldn't that mean the custom element has to implement reference counting? And even then the `OpaqueRange` could be handed out through various libraries, some of which might call `disconnect()` whereas others wanted to hold onto it still. We no-opped `detach()` on `Range`. It's unclear this is needed, especially for a v0.

I don't think `OpaqueRange` should inherit from `AbstractRange` anymore. And if we're going to have fake offsets instead of using it as a token exchange (which I'd prefer as I think it's more elegant), we should own that and make it clear in the API. Just have `start` end `end` as integers. That makes it clear this is a bit distinct from `Range`, both for consumers and producers.

A controller object seems reasonable. The other shape I thought of would be to do something similar to the revealing constructor pattern of promises: `new OpaqueRange(controller => controller.doSomething())`. I'm not actually sure why we didn't do that for `AbortSignal`. Maybe @jakearchibald remembers?

And obviously colleagues and I continue to feel strongly we should have a design that works for custom elements and more importantly works for making arbitrary ranges opaque, not just ranges where the start end end node is the same `Text` node. But I think something along the above lines would do that.
To add, your `OpaqueRangeController` object design appears incomplete. You need control over the start node, start offset, start fake offset, end node, end offset, and end fake offset.

@stephanieyzhang could you also make sure this discussion is linked from one of the DOM standard issues? As a lot of this will end up in the DOM standard so we really want that community's input, even though there's significant overlap.
They can create custom objects, but those won't work with the Highlight API or other APIs consuming ranges, as already discussed.

@smaug----, @keithamus, @annevk, @LeaVerou: Quick check on what was discussed at the 5/28 meeting before I draft the IDL changes -- please correct me if I have this wrong:

- `startOffset` and `endOffset` are removed from `AbstractRange` and moved into a new mixin (something like `RangeOffsets`)
- `Range` and `StaticRange` include the mixin (no behavior change for them)
- `OpaqueRange` still inherits from `AbstractRange` (so it remains usable with the Highlight API), but does **not** include the mixin. Instead it exposes plain integer `start` and `end` attributes, to make clear they're a different concept from the mixin's offsets.

I created https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1469 to make `AbstractRange` empty a couple of days ago. I'd appreciate review. As Olli noted in Chat there is a slight compatibility risk, but usually moving APIs around like that has been fine so I suspect the same applies here.

And yeah, that's what I'd envision for `OpaqueRange` on top of that.

There was some further bikeshedding on my PR on Chat with two suggested paths forward:

- 🎉 Keep `AbstractRange` as-is, add `OpaqueRange` as standalone interface, and use `typedef (AbstractRange or OpaqueRange) AnyRange;` for the Highlight API.
- 🚀 Move both container attributes and `collapsed` from `AbstractRange` to `NodeRange`, which will inherit from `AbstractRange`, and make `StaticRange` and `Range` both inherit from `NodeRange`. Then `OpaqueRange` can inherit from `AbstractRange`.

Maybe we can give people a couple of days to pick between these? If there's time we can also discuss more today. I'm happy to figure out the required changes for this.
(I think collapsed could stay in AbstractRange. It would be effectively startOffset == endOffset for OpaqueRange.)
